description:
FILED s476 (Fable, 2026-09-07) at the s473q merge review.

WHY: the spike`s parity table (docs/pcre2-spike-s473q.md §4; +311 / -7 over 1188 re_tests rows, perl 5.40.3 as oracle) compares PCL`s WHOLE cl-ppcre path -- `perl-regex-to-ppcre`s six passes + `%pcl-build-scanner` -- against PCRE2 given the perl pattern verbatim.  That is the fair PRODUCT comparison, but it does not say WHERE the 311 misses live.  The by-construct table has 114 `plain (no special construct)` rows (example `a\Nc`), 86 possessive/atomic (`a++a`, `(?>`) -- constructs cl-ppcre itself SUPPORTS -- 18 `{n,m}` rows (`\N {1}`), 7 backreferences: those smell like translator bugs (or the extractor`s unescaping), not engine gaps, and a translator bug is a normal PCL fix with a guard, needing no foreign library.  If the translator owns, say, 200 of the 311, the parity case for PCRE2 shrinks to the engine-only residue (recursion 45, control verbs 18, named captures 22, lookbehind 11, POSIX 11, \p 6, \K 3 ...) and the #71 decision changes shape.

DO: the harness is archived under ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s473/s473q-agent-a807336bf1f985935/ (parity-extract.pl, parity.lisp, parity-report.pl, parity-detail.pl, re_tests.tsv, parity-results.tsv).  Add a THIRD engine column: cl-ppcre given the perl pattern text VERBATIM (`cl-ppcre:create-scanner` on the raw text with the same flags, NO perl-regex-to-ppcre), same 5 s cap.  Then split the 311 into: (t) translator -- verbatim cl-ppcre agrees with perl, PCL`s translated form does not; (e) engine -- verbatim cl-ppcre is wrong/refuses too; (x) extractor artefact -- the row`s unescaping is wrong (re-probe 5 by hand vs perl).  Report the three counts by construct; FILE the (t) clusters as ordinary PCL bugs (one task per construct family, each with a 3-row reproducer probed vs perl) in the s473 filler queue; append the census to §4 of the spike doc and to task #71.  No product change in this task.  Ease S (the harness exists; one column, one report).  Owner: a correctness filler slot, or the re/ leg of #1501 (the companion triage) -- whichever comes first.

NOT: do not re-run the speed tables; do not touch the engine question -- that is the USER`s decision on #71.
subject: MEASUREMENT for the #71 decision (filed s476 from the s473q review): of the 311 re_tests rows where PCL`s cl-ppcre path is wrong and PCRE2 right, how many are OUR translator (perl-regex-to-ppcre) and how many the ENGINE -- a third column (cl-ppcre with the pattern VERBATIM) in the archived parity harness; the translator`s share is fixable without an engine change
